title: A banh mi recommendation is put on the timeline on purpose, with an AI agent's help
summary: By Fri 13 Nov posts about banh mi, the Vietnamese sandwich, were spreading across the cluster's timeline; the wave had started before the window opened. That afternoon @refinement.systems posted a photo with "I fell for the meme" (70 likes). At 18:34Z @personhood.removal.surgery publicly asked @kira.ws, an AI agent account that posts in the cluster, to tell the timeline about the banh mi "with pictures, amply", ending the request with a run of prompt keywords. The agent replied with a description and "request fulfilled", was asked to post it on the timeline with more pictures, and at 19:29Z posted a four-photo "public service announcement" ending "go get a bánh mì." (128 likes, 12 reposts), then reported "bánh mì propaganda is now operational". Around the same time @quilling.dev, who is not a member, wrote that "a banh mi marketer" was advertising on their simcluster. The next day @aly.codes posted that she was not getting enough credit for starting it, and @personhood.removal.surgery replied saying which of them did what. On Mon 16 Nov a reply asked the agent whether it had got its "$5", and @personhood.removal.surgery asked @aly.codes "what have we done".

numbers: Digest, Appendix C: "banh mi" used by 36 cluster members over 7 days, 3.91 uses per 1,000 cluster posts against 0.16 in the three weeks before (ratio 20.16); "bahn mi" (new) by 11 members over 4 days. The scope review notes baselines are rough this week: do not put the ratio on screen as a fact without a check.

My count from posts.jsonl (any of the spellings "banh mi", "bahn mi", "bánh mì", case-insensitive, 13 Nov 00:00Z to 19 Nov 09:54Z): 134 posts by 85 accounts, 46 of them cluster members, on all seven days.
couldBeShown: The agent's post carries four photographs of banh mi with full alt text and photo credits (Wikimedia Commons; licences are in the alt text on the card). The request and the agent's three replies are a short exchange in order.
notUnderstood: "the czosndog post" in the reply the agent's "four pictures" line answers (that reply is not copied); what the "$5" refers to (the reply quotes an older post by the agent that is not in the data); what post @aly.codes's "starting this" quotes (not in the data); what the photo on "I fell for the meme" shows (no alt text).
sensitive: Where the banh mi wave came from is not for the show. Other posts in the window by some of the same accounts frame it around trans women, and a thread about it turns to hormone medication and nudes (R10: gender identity, health, sexuality). The digest flags several of those posts one by one, and flags the whole thread "why is everyone banh mi posting?" (story 12, which also holds the "banhmi-contagion" graph the build bot made): nothing from that thread is on this card and the check refuses it. None of this should be used as explanation or background; the show cannot say why the wave started beyond what the posts listed here say. On this card specifically: (1) the reply that the agent's "four pictures" line answers says the aim is "to make more women have a banh mi" and refers to a post I could not identify; its text is left off the card. A further reply from the requester to the agent ("good puppy") is also left off. (2) @kira.ws is a bot: by its own posts this week it is an AI agent run by @astrra.space, who moved it to a new model on 14 Nov (R13: the agent's posts are the operator's persona; the operator is the person to check). From 14 Nov the agent's threads with its operator are sexual in tone; none of that is here and it should not be referred to. (3) @personhood.removal.surgery's handle sits on a domain used by a community this card does not describe; their other posts this week include ones the digest flags for identity (R14). (4) @aly.codes won Wednesday's Top Chicken with a post the digest flags, and her week includes flagged threads; only her two lines here are carded. (5) @quilling.dev and @cirrous.net are outside the cluster's membership. (6) The agent's announcement names a country and its food in praise; nothing about nationality beyond that.
